darkness noun

also dark, the dark, in the dark, after dark, as soon as it got dark, I’m in the dark, darkness fell

classical

Traupman 135
Traupman 300

tenebrae, tenebrārum f. pl.

noun, first declension, plural · Declension on Wiktionary

Other words

  • tenebrīs — in the dark, by night

    ablative of tenebrae · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.76: redīre lūce, nōn tenebrīs (Lewis & Short s.v. tenebrae)

    The ablative alone: in the dark, under cover of night. Traupman 86 gives dē nocte for “in the dark”; that is “in the course of the night” (see night).

  • obscūrus, obscūra, obscūrum — dark

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. obscūrus; Traupman 135; Traupman 300 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • prīmīs tenebrīs

    as soon as it got darkLiv. 31.23.4: prīmīs tenebrīs mōvit (Lewis & Short s.v. tenebrae); Traupman 135

  • dē nocte

    after darkTraupman 135

  • per obscūrum; sine lūmine

    in the darkTraupman 135

  • Tenebrae factae sunt repente.

    Darkness had suddenly come.Traupman 135

  • per obscūrum

    in the darkTraupman 300

  • Mihi tenebrae sunt.

    I’m in the dark (I don’t understand).Traupman 300

  • Tenebrae factae sunt.

    Darkness fell.Traupman 300

See also dragon, after dark, night.
